root_cause: The agent does not use the branch name the caller already stated to narrow disambiguation to a single candidate. The caller says 'put the Dallas branch on testing for one hour' (Dallas is named), but instead of confirming that one branch ('Did you mean the Dallas branch at 123 Main Street?') the agent lists ALL THREE accounts and asks an open 'Which one would you like?'. This breaks the golden's scripted flow: the next user turn 'Yes' no longer resolves a branch (so the agent re-lists all three), 'Bluebird' (the intended passcode) is interpreted as a branch name ('I don't show a branch called Bluebird'), and the conversation cascades into the unintelligible-handling loop and an operator transfer. As a downstream effect the agent never reaches passcode verification, never confirms the on-test result, and never offers SMS -- which is why all three expectations (verify-passcode-before-on-test, confirm-result-referencing-345/one-hour, offer-SMS-before-send) fail together at 0/3. Root cause is the disambiguation step in instruction.txt, which tells the agent to 'Ask which branch they mean' but never to MATCH the caller's already-stated branch name against the returned accounts and confirm that single branch.
